evals.prompt: We're a two-person startup creating our first icon set: about 20 product UI icons plus a few larger marketing icons for the landing page. Give us concrete rules for icon sizing, color, and stroke treatment, and the right way to produce each icon at multiple sizes.
evals.expected_output: Icon guidelines matching the skill: one 24px base size with sizes at multiples of 8 (16/24/32), 1-color product icons and max 2-color marketing icons, uniform stroke weight with stroke gaps at least the stroke weight, and building the large size first then simplifying down.
expectations: Recommends picking a single base icon size (24px named, or sizes restricted to 16/24/32 as multiples of 8), adding other sizes only when glyph complexity requires it
States product icons should use exactly 1 color and marketing icons at most 2 colors, noting 3+ colors reads as illustration rather than icon
Directs building the large size first and simplifying down for smaller sizes — never designing the small size first
Requires all strokes in a set to share one weight and warns against mixing filled and stroked icons side by side without intention

States the gap between strokes must be at least the stroke weight, or that edge padding equal to the stroke weight balances visual weight (or aligning straight lines to the pixel grid with an optical grid for perceptual center)

evals.prompt: Our design system team is stuck in a naming war over a new overlay component — half want to call it Popup, half Dialog — and it seems to overlap with our existing Modal and Tooltip components. What process should we follow to define this component properly so this stops happening?
evals.expected_output: A purpose-first definition process: write a 1–2 sentence design rationale before any naming, involve designer/developer/content strategist/maintainer, derive the name from the agreed purpose, distinguish it from Modal/Tooltip by documented purpose rather than visuals, and document do/don't usage with states and variants.
expectations: Instructs writing a 1–2 sentence purpose statement / design rationale as the FIRST step, before choosing any name
States that naming (and behavior) follows naturally once the purpose is agreed — the rationale is the source of truth for naming and future evolution
Says semantically similar components (e.g., modal vs. prompt/popup vs. popover/tooltip) must be distinguished by documented purpose, not visual appearance
Recommends involving multiple disciplines in the definition — designer, developer, and content strategist and/or maintainer
Calls for usage documentation including do/don't examples plus states and variants

evals.prompt: Product teams at my company keep quietly shipping modified copies of our design-system components, and our documentation no longer matches what's in production. How should we set up governance and a contribution process for the design system?
evals.expected_output: A documented contribution model naming who can propose/review/approve, a clear owner per component, a self-governing process built from proposal format + design rationale + review checklist + merge criteria, ambiguity resolved at the component definition stage, and regular audits comparing the system to production.
expectations: Prescribes documenting a contribution model that specifies who can propose, who reviews, and who approves
Assigns each component a clear owner
Enumerates the requirements of a self-governing contribution process: proposal format, design rationale, review checklist, and merge criteria
Attributes compliance problems to ambiguous documentation and says to resolve them at the component definition stage, not after the fact
Recommends regular audits comparing the design system to what is actually in production
